rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wish follows the soul’s admission of falsehood and resort to fabrication, adding a futile wish that only increases its loss.
rows.anchor: فقال : { أو تقول } أي تلك النفس المفرطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heedless soul wishes for a return to the abode of deeds so it can act and become one of those who do good.
rows.anchor: أي رجعة إلى دار العمل لأتمكن منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He parses “so I might be” as coordinated with the response to the wish; this parsing best fits the following verses.
rows.anchor: هذا الإعراب - وهو عطفه على الجواب - أوفق لبقية الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Indeed” refutes the excuses: both clear revelation and an opportunity to act had reached the soul.
rows.anchor: أي قد كان لك الأمران كلاهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to God’s first-person speech without an explicit majestic title signals the culmination of wrath; the prior address exposed the soul’s weakness under punishment.
rows.anchor: إعلاما بتناهي الغضب بعد لفته إلى تذكير النفس المخاطبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs were exceptionally clear and arrived when the person could act with heart, tongue, and limbs.
rows.anchor: في وقت كنت فيه متمكنا من العمل بالجنان واللسان والأركان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person denied the signs audaciously and counted himself too great to accept them; ingrained pride, not missing proof or time, prevented good action.
rows.anchor: جرأة على الله وقلة مبالاة بالعواقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording portrays disbelief as deeply entrenched, as though a disposition: the person persistently concealed guidance and denied it out of pride.
rows.anchor: كونا كأنه جبلة لك لشدة توغلك فيه وحرصك عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seek God’s protection from the harm of the disputants’ pride, as Moses sought refuge, so God may fulfill His promise as He did for Moses.
rows.anchor: كما عاذ به موسى عليه السلام لينجز لك ما وعدك كما أنجز له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone hears everything that can be heard.
rows.anchor: أي وحده { السميع } لكل ما يمكن أن يسمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “All-seeing” covers perception by sight and insight into what is known; the context concerns human devils with overt and hidden schemes.
rows.anchor: الصالح للبصر والبصيرة فيعم المحسوس والمعلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike al-Aʿraf and Fussilat, whose endings follow Satanic insinuation and end with “All-knowing,” this passage ends with “All-seeing” to match its context.
rows.anchor: وختم آيتي الأعراف وفصلت المسبوقتين لنزغ الشيطان الذي هو وساس

words: لخلق السماوات والأرض أكبر من خلق الناس
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scale of the heavens and earth answers disputants’ denial of resurrection and points to the final gathering, judgment, and vindication of prophets and followers.
rows.anchor: أعظم النظر في آية المجادلة المكررة من أول السورة إلى هنا إلى البعث

words: لخلق السماوات والأرض أكبر من خلق الناس
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who can originate the immense heavens and earth can certainly recreate people, whose creation is comparatively slight.
rows.anchor: الذي قدر على ابتدائه على عظمه قادر على إعادة الناس على حقارتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most deniers fail to infer resurrection from creation; they see externals like animals but fail to grasp the obvious inward implication.
rows.anchor: فهم لا يستدلون بذلك على القدرة على البعث كما أن البهائم ترى الظاهر

words: لخلق السماوات والأرض أكبر من خلق الناس
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The differences among people disprove that their creation derives from blind natural causes; the heavens and earth would produce equal outcomes if unchoosing natures caused them. Pharaoh had held such a view.
rows.anchor: ومن هؤلاء فرعون الذي مضى في هذه السورة كثير من كشف عواره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Observable differences show that creation depends on a freely choosing, unique creator rather than nature; the unequal blind and sighted provide a further example.
rows.anchor: فدل ذلك قطعا على أنها غير مستندة إلى طبيعة بل إلى فاعل مختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After physical darkness and light, the verse turns to spiritual darkness and light; the guided are rare, like refined gold among coins.
rows.anchor: أتبعه المعنويين نشرا ليكشف قسما الظلام قسمي النور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe and do righteous deeds are people of excellence, in contrast with the wrongdoer.
rows.anchor: أي أوجدوا هذه الحقيقة ثبتت أو لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The varied conjunctions distinguish the intended comparisons: the wording denies equality between blind and sighted, and between believers who excel and wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: المراد - والله أعلم - نفس التساوي بين أفراد الأعمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sighted is joined without an added “no” because the apparent contrast between types is clear, while denying equality among individuals within types is subtler.
rows.anchor: عطف البصير بغير ( لا ) ليكون ظاهر ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only a plain conjunction precedes the believers because no one would confuse the believing group with the blind or suppose its members equal to them.
rows.anchor: واقتصر على الواو في عطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding “no” and using the singular “wrongdoer” signals that equality is denied among individuals of each kind, underscoring God’s freely chosen creation.
rows.anchor: وزيدت ( لا ) في المسيء وعبر فيه بالإفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī contrasts this wording with Fatir 35:19: without “no” there, readers might wrongly take darkness as equal to the blind and sighted, since darkness varies in density.
rows.anchor: وهذا بخلاف الظلمات في سورة فاطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ellipsis by cross-reference: righteous deeds first imply their opposite, while the wrongdoer later implies the good-doer; this encourages goodness and warns against sin.
rows.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : ذكر عمل الصالحات أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kufan readers have the second-person reading “you remember”; Biqāʿī says direct address rebukes more sharply and signals greater anger.
rows.anchor: على قراءة الكوفيين بالخطاب لأنه أقوى في التبكيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Few of the disputants—or people generally—take heed; the author allows the rebuke to address either them or people at large.
rows.anchor: أي المجادلون أو أيها المجادلون أو الناس

words: إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ لَآتِيَةٌ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour must come so God can judge justly between wrongdoer and doer of good, since wisdom forbids treating them alike and worldly injustice remains unresolved.
rows.anchor: للحكم بالعدل في المقارنة بين المسيء والمحسن لأنه لا يسوغ في الحكمة

words: إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ لَآتِيَةٌ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People see sinners enjoying ease, obedient people suffering, and the oppressed awaiting vindication; the afterlife completes the justice absent from these scenes.
rows.anchor: والمحسن وهو في غاية البلاء والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse denies faith rather than knowledge: most people do not trust the messenger despite the Hour’s obvious evidence, through obstinacy or confinement to sensory perception.
rows.anchor: أي لا يجعلون المخبر لهم بإيتانها آمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Call on Me” means respond to God by worshiping Him alone and asking for promised victory; worshipful submission by supplication, prayer, or otherwise counts as supplication.
rows.anchor: استجيبوا لي بأن تعبدوني وحدي فتسألوني ما وعدتكم به من النصرة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet’s saying “supplication is worship” supports Biqāʿī’s broad reading of supplication as encompassing worship.
rows.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( الدعاء هو العبادة )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the command as “affirm My oneness, and I will forgive you.”
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : وحدوني اغفر لكم

rows.speaker: الثوري
rows.claim: When al-Thawrī was asked to supplicate, he replied that abandoning sins is itself supplication.
rows.anchor: وعن الثوري أنه قيل له : ادع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may answer by granting the requested thing in this world, removing a comparable harm, or reserving the reward for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا أي بإيجاد ما دعوتم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This promise parallels God’s assurance that He answers the caller who calls upon Him in al-Baqara 2:186.
rows.anchor: والآية بمعنى آية البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People must not rely on the promise and abandon supplication, since supplication is the core of worship and each person is enabled for what they were created to do.
rows.anchor: ولا تتكلوا على ما سبق به الوعد فتتركوا الدعاء

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī is cited for the saying that supplication is the key to response and lawful food its teeth.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري , وقيل : الدعاء مفتاح الإجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pride is a usual cause of abandoning supplication, so the threat warns against refusing the call to worship while implicitly encouraging prayer.
rows.anchor: ولما كان السبب في ترك الدعاء في العادة الكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being too proud for worship means refusing God’s call, disputing His signs, and turning away from calling upon Him in hardship and ease.
rows.anchor: عن الاستجابة لي فيما دعوت من العبادة بالمجادلة في آياتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They enter Hell under a certain promise, humbled and abased as fitting recompense for their pride.
rows.anchor: أي صاغرين حقيرين ذليلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ellipsis by cross-reference: mentioning supplication first implies its omission later, while worship mentioned later implies its omission at first.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : ذكر الدعاء أولا دليلا على حذفه ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night and day signs reinforce that the Creator will not neglect creation: a perfectly ordered world of work leads to reckoning, reward, and punishment.
rows.anchor: زاد في الدلالة عليه وعلى الفعل بالاختيار والحكمة التي لا يسوغ معها إهمال الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night brings outward rest through sleep, a minor death, and true rest through worship, the enduring life.
rows.anchor: راحة ظاهرية بالنوم الذي هو الموت الأصغر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Day enables movement through wakefulness, which is life in meaning.
rows.anchor: لتنتشروا فيه باليقظة التي هي إحياء في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night-and-day description uses ellipsis: darkness is omitted because illumination is the intended blessing, and spreading by day follows from sight; night’s chief benefit is rest.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : حذف الظلام أولا لكونه ليس من النعم المقصودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against those who assign events to nature without choice, God is the possessor of abundant, freely bestowed favor through the alternation of night and day.
rows.anchor: بعض الكفرة ينسب الأفعال كما مضى للطبائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people fail to thank God because they ignorantly attribute His acts to others and act in ways that strip them of gratitude, including associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: فينسبون أفعاله سبحانه إلى غيره جهلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī allows “people” first to mean every existent being, and in its second occurrence to mean jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد بالناس أولا كل من يتأتى منه النوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After signs in heaven, some of which are worshiped, the passage turns to earthly signs; unlike Yasin, the context here emphasizes oneness, while Yasin stresses resurrection and the earth’s proof is clearer there.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر بعض آيات السماء لشرفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One sees part of the earth directly and apprehends the rest by reasoning from what is visible, since all of it is equally within divine power.
rows.anchor: أي بعضها بحاسة البصر وبعضها بعين البصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is “humble” when dry and bare of vegetation, like a powerless, flattened person.
rows.anchor: أي يابسة لا نبات فيها فهي بصورة الذليل الذي لا منعة عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says this depiction is closer to the worshipper’s state than the description previously used in al-Hajj.
rows.anchor: عبر بما هو أقرب إلى حال العابد ما مضى في الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s sending of rain is exclusively His act and one of the strongest signs of the One; the switch to the majestic plural signals power and greatness.
rows.anchor: إنزال الماء مما استأثر به سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain may come from clouds or be driven from high places, bringing soil suitable for growth even to saline land such as Egypt.
rows.anchor: من الغمام أو سقناه إليها من الأماكن العالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth “shakes” by moving greatly, abundantly, and quickly, as though it were doing this of its own accord.
rows.anchor: تحركت حركة عظيمة كثير سريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth cracks and rises; plants emerge, cover its face, branch roots, and thicken stems until passage across it is impeded.
rows.anchor: تشققت فارتفع ترابها وخرج منها النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an inward allusion, knowledge waters the soul-earth: remorse bears blessings, shortcomings are pardoned, and obedience, nearness, and divine manifestations adorn and purify it.
rows.anchor: فطرها بمياه المعارف فظهرت فيها بركات الندم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The visible revival of earth proves power to bring the nonexistent into being and restore what decayed and crumbled; reviving the dead is no different.
rows.anchor: دليلا مشاهدا على القدرة على إيجاد المعدوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God revives the dead just as He brings forth plants after they decayed and became soil.
rows.anchor: الذي كان بلي وتحطم وصار ترابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although people acknowledge God’s complete power, their denial of resurrection treats Him as unable; all possible things are equally within complete power.
rows.anchor: الممكنات متساوية الأقدام بالنسبة إلى القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the call to God is the greatest office and resurrection one of the strongest proofs of oneness, the passage now threatens those who reject it; its wording addresses the Prophet and others generally.
rows.anchor: أن الدعوة إلى الله أعظم المناصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who commit ilḥād turn meanings away from their proper aim and the just path.
rows.anchor: أي يميلون بصرف المعاني عن القصد وسنن العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An example is the claim that idols are worshiped only to bring their worshipers nearer to God.
rows.anchor: قولهم { ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilḥād also includes futile obstruction through noise, whistling, clapping, and every form of distraction from the truth.
rows.anchor: أو يماحلون باللغو بالمكاء والتصدية وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī links Noah’s promise of forgiveness, abundant rain, and wealth with this passage’s teaching about God’s provision and governance.
rows.anchor: استغفروا ربكم إنه كان غفارا يرسل السماء عليكم مدرارا ويمددكم بأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited promise that believers who do good enter gardens connects faith and righteous action with divine reward.
rows.anchor: ومن يؤمن بالله ويعمل صالحا يدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited promise to believing, God-fearing communities of blessings from heaven and earth supports the passage’s account of provision.
rows.anchor: ولو أن أهل القرى آمنوا واتقوا لفتحنا عليهم بركات من السماء والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage is also linked to the promise that upholding the Torah and Gospel brings provision from above and below.
rows.anchor: ولو أنهم أقاموا التوراة والإنجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s all-encompassing knowledge explains His acts: each follows the most exact laws of wisdom, with wisdoms beyond the grasp of even the most excellent peoples.
rows.anchor: فلا فعل له إلا وهو جار على أتقن ما يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī argues that had God expanded and empowered the Arabs and then granted them Persian and Roman rule, they would have accepted it through their strength and capacity.
rows.anchor: فلو أنه وسع العرب وقواهم ثم أباحهم ملك أهل فارس والروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God alone governs existence, He alone lays down the paths of religion, the greatest provision; He legislated the shared religion upheld by the prophets.
rows.anchor: وأنه لا متصرف في الوجود سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He legislated” means He laid down a clear, manifest path for the final community.
rows.anchor: أي طرق وسن طريقا ظاهرا بينا واضحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religion here is what people practice and are recompensed for.
rows.anchor: وهو ما يعمل فيجازى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is named first as the earliest messenger forefather sent to dissenters; the same religion runs from him through the final Prophet and intervening famous prophets.
rows.anchor: ذكر لهم أول الآباء المرسلين إلى المخالفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Arabs reject the religion as new, Biqāʿī argues it is actually the oldest; every prophet came with it and innate human nature bears witness, even in hardship.
rows.anchor: فإن كنتم إنما تأنفون من الدخول في هذا الدين لحدوثه فإنه أقدم الأديان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic revelation to Muhammad is singled out with “We revealed” and placed before earlier prophets; its full meaning is uniquely grasped by him.
rows.anchor: أبرزه في مظهر العظمة معبرا بالوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī distinguishes Muhammad’s revelation from the others’ enjoinment, presenting it as greater; he also marks Abraham’s honor through the majestic plural.
rows.anchor: ودل على عظمه ما كان لإبراهيم وبنيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham was saved from Nimrod’s plot and fire and given Ishmael and Isaac in old age; as a leading ancestor of the Arabs, he should be followed.
rows.anchor: نجيناه من كيد نمرود بالنار وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses received the Torah as admonition and an explanation of everything.
rows.anchor: أنزلنا عليه التوراة موعظة وتفصيلا لكل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus received the Gospel containing guidance, light, and admonition; God preserved him in heaven for the law of the final Prophet.
rows.anchor: ودخرناه في سمائنا شريعة الخاتم الفاتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That you establish the religion” may substitute for the object of “He legislated,” or begin a new sentence; “that” may be a verbal noun or explanatory after wording that implies speech.
rows.anchor: أبرزه في أسلوب الأمر فقال مبدلا من معمول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All final and earlier communities are commanded to establish the religion: return to primordial monotheism, affirm every perfection of God, and uphold what His messengers conveyed.
rows.anchor: بالرجوع إلى ما فطروا عليه وقت الاضطرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added tāʾ in the prohibition signals emphatic, grave division; Biqāʿī suggests warning against division in fundamentals while allowing some subsidiary interpretation.
rows.anchor: تفرقا عظيما بما أشار إليه إثبات التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Communities should preserve unity in ease as well as hardship; division brings ruin, unity brings deliverance, so the People of the Book should be one hand.
rows.anchor: النداة , فكونوا يدا واحدة يا أهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī reinforces unity by quoting the call to the People of the Book to agree on a common word: worship God alone and take no lords besides Him.
rows.anchor: يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to unite on God’s oneness weighs heavily on the polytheists and constricts their chests, so they seek to divide believers; division sides with the envious enemy against God.
rows.anchor: حتى ضاقت به صدورهم , وهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although polytheists resist the call, God can bring anyone He wills into the religion; the shift to God’s name emphasizes His power over every heart.
rows.anchor: كيف السبيل مع ذلك إلى دخول أحد في هذا الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Chooses” means selecting with utmost care and drawing the chosen person toward the religion.
rows.anchor: يختار بغاية العناية ويصرف { إليه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides the one who turns back by enabling obedience; such a person is ready to renew inward return to obedience at every moment while progressing through its stations.
rows.anchor: بالتوفيق للطاعة { من ينيب * } أي فيه أهلية
